front: Je suis ravi que vous soyez venus.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee rah-vee kuh voo swah-yay vuh-NÜ]
back: I'm delighted you came.
context: Past subjunctive = subjunctive of être/avoir + participle. Used for an action completed before the main verb.

front: Je regrette que tu n'aies pas pu assister à la réunion.
pronunciation: [zhuh ruh-gret kuh tü neh pah pü ah-sees-tay ah lah ray-ü-NYOHN]
back: I'm sorry you couldn't attend the meeting.
context: Regret + past subjunctive.

front: Il faut que tu aies fini avant midi.
pronunciation: [eel foh kuh tü eh fee-NEE ah-vahn mee-DEE]
back: You need to have finished before noon.
context: Past subjunctive for an action to be completed by a deadline.

front: Bien qu'il ait beaucoup travaillé, il a raté l'examen.
pronunciation: [byan keel eh boh-koo trah-vah-YAY, ee lah rah-tay leg-zah-MAN]
back: Although he had worked hard, he failed the exam.
context: 'Bien que' + past subjunctive.

front: Je doute qu'elle ait reçu mon message.
pronunciation: [zhuh doot kel eh ruh-SÜ mohn meh-SAHZH]
back: I doubt she received my message.
context: Doubt about a past event → past subjunctive.

front: C'est le meilleur livre que j'aie jamais lu.
pronunciation: [seh luh meh-yuhr LEE-vruh kuh zhay zhah-meh LÜ]
back: It's the best book I've ever read.
context: Superlative + que + past subjunctive.

front: Je ne pense pas qu'ils soient déjà arrivés.
pronunciation: [zhuh nuh pahns pah keel swah day-zhah zah-ree-VAY]
back: I don't think they've arrived yet.
context: Être verbs in the past subjunctive: qu'ils soient arrivés (agreement).

front: Quand je suis arrivé, le film avait déjà commencé.
pronunciation: [kahn zhuh swee zah-ree-VAY, luh feelm ah-veh day-zhah koh-mahn-SAY]
back: When I arrived, the film had already started.
context: Plus-que-parfait = imparfait of avoir/être + participle: an action before another past action.

front: Elle était fatiguée parce qu'elle avait mal dormi.
pronunciation: [el ay-teh fah-tee-GAY pars kel ah-veh mahl dor-MEE]
back: She was tired because she had slept badly.
context: Plus-que-parfait gives the earlier cause.

front: Nous étions partis avant la tempête.
pronunciation: [noo zay-tyohn par-TEE ah-vahn lah tahm-PET]
back: We had left before the storm.
context: Être verbs: étions partis.

front: Si j'avais su, je serais venu plus tôt.
pronunciation: [see zhah-veh SÜ, zhuh suh-reh vuh-nü plü TOH]
back: If I had known, I'd have come earlier.
context: Si + plus-que-parfait → past conditional (regret about the past).

front: Si tu m'avais écouté, on ne serait pas perdus.
pronunciation: [see tü mah-veh zay-koo-TAY, ohn nuh suh-reh pah pehr-DÜ]
back: If you'd listened to me, we wouldn't be lost.
context: Mixed: past condition, present consequence.

front: Il m'a dit qu'il était malade.
pronunciation: [eel mah dee keel ay-teh mah-LAD]
back: He told me he was ill.
context: Reported speech: present ('je suis malade') → imparfait after a past verb.

front: Elle a dit qu'elle viendrait demain.
pronunciation: [el ah dee kel vyan-dreh duh-MAN]
back: She said she would come tomorrow.
context: Future ('je viendrai') → conditional in reported speech.

front: Il m'a expliqué qu'il avait perdu ses clés.
pronunciation: [eel mah ek-splee-kay keel ah-veh pehr-dü say KLAY]
back: He explained he had lost his keys.
context: Passé composé ('j'ai perdu') → plus-que-parfait.

front: Elle m'a demandé si j'avais faim.
pronunciation: [el mah duh-mahn-day see zhah-veh FAN]
back: She asked me if I was hungry.
context: Yes/no questions are reported with 'si'.

front: Il voulait savoir où j'habitais.
pronunciation: [eel voo-leh sah-vwahr oo zhah-bee-TEH]
back: He wanted to know where I lived.
context: Question words stay: où, quand, comment, pourquoi.

front: Elle m'a demandé ce que je faisais.
pronunciation: [el mah duh-mahn-day suh kuh zhuh fuh-ZEH]
back: She asked me what I was doing.
context: 'Qu'est-ce que' → 'ce que' in reported speech.

front: Il m'a demandé ce qui s'était passé.
pronunciation: [eel mah duh-mahn-day suh kee seh-teh pah-SAY]
back: He asked me what had happened.
context: 'Qu'est-ce qui' → 'ce qui'.

front: Le professeur nous a dit de fermer nos livres.
pronunciation: [luh proh-feh-suhr noo zah dee duh fehr-may noh LEE-vruh]
back: The teacher told us to close our books.
context: Reported command: dire de + infinitive.

front: Il m'a dit qu'il me rappellerait le lendemain.
pronunciation: [eel mah dee keel muh rah-pel-reh luh lahn-duh-MAN]
back: He told me he would call me back the next day.
context: Time words change: demain → le lendemain, hier → la veille, aujourd'hui → ce jour-là.

front: Elle a affirmé qu'elle était passée la veille.
pronunciation: [el ah ah-feer-may kel ay-teh pah-say lah VAY]
back: She claimed she had come by the day before.
context: 'La veille' = the day before.

front: Il a annoncé qu'il démissionnait.
pronunciation: [ee lah ah-noh-say keel day-mee-syoh-NEH]
back: He announced he was resigning.
context: Reporting verbs: affirmer, annoncer, déclarer, expliquer, prétendre.

front: Je savais que tu réussirais.
pronunciation: [zhuh sah-veh kuh tü ray-ü-see-REH]
back: I knew you would succeed.
context: Future in the past → conditional.

front: Il pensait que nous serions partis avant midi.
pronunciation: [eel pahn-seh kuh noo suh-ryohn par-tee ah-vahn mee-DEE]
back: He thought we would have left before noon.
context: Past conditional as future perfect in the past.

front: J'aurais voulu que tu sois là.
pronunciation: [zhoh-reh voo-lü kuh tü swah LAH]
back: I would have liked you to be there.
context: Main verb in the past conditional + subjunctive.

front: Il fallait que je parte tôt.
pronunciation: [eel fah-leh kuh zhuh PART TOH]
back: I had to leave early.
context: In modern French, the present subjunctive is used even after a past main verb.

front: Il fallait qu'il partît.
pronunciation: [eel fah-leh keel par-TEE]
back: He had to leave. (literary)
context: The imperfect subjunctive ('partît') appears only in literature. Recognize it, don't use it in speech.

front: Après avoir dîné, nous sommes sortis.
pronunciation: [ah-preh zah-vwahr dee-NAY, noo sum sor-TEE]
back: After having dinner, we went out.
context: 'Après' + past infinitive (avoir/être + participle), when the subject is the same.

front: Après être rentrée, elle s'est couchée.
pronunciation: [ah-preh zeh-truh rahn-TRAY, el seh koo-SHAY]
back: After getting home, she went to bed.
context: Être verbs agree in the past infinitive: être rentrée.

front: Je te remercie de m'avoir aidé.
pronunciation: [zhuh tuh ruh-mehr-SEE duh mah-vwahr eh-DAY]
back: Thank you for helping me.
context: 'Remercier de' + past infinitive (the help came before the thanks).

front: Il regrette d'être parti si vite.
pronunciation: [eel ruh-gret deh-truh par-tee see VEET]
back: He regrets leaving so quickly.
context: Past infinitive after regretter de.

front: Une fois le travail terminé, on ira boire un verre.
pronunciation: [ün FWAH luh trah-vahy tehr-mee-NAY, ohn nee-rah bwahr an VEHR]
back: Once the work is done, we'll go for a drink.
context: 'Une fois' + noun + participle = once (done).

front: Dès qu'il eut fini, il quitta la pièce.
pronunciation: [deh keel ü fee-NEE, eel kee-tah lah PYES]
back: As soon as he had finished, he left the room.
context: Passé antérieur + passé simple: literary narrative tenses. Recognize them in novels.

front: Le président a déclaré qu'il ferait tout son possible.
pronunciation: [luh pray-zee-dahn ah day-klah-ray keel fuh-reh too sohn poh-SEE-bluh]
back: The president declared he would do everything possible.
context: Typical news-report sentence.

front: Elle prétend qu'elle n'a rien vu.
pronunciation: [el pray-tahn kel nah ryan VÜ]
back: She claims she saw nothing.
context: Present reporting verb → no tense change. False friend: 'prétendre' = to claim, not to pretend.

front: On m'a dit que la boutique avait fermé.
pronunciation: [ohn mah dee kuh lah boo-teek ah-veh fehr-MAY]
back: I was told the shop had closed.
context: 'On m'a dit que' = I was told that.

front: Je ne savais pas que vous vous connaissiez.
pronunciation: [zhuh nuh sah-veh pah kuh voo voo koh-neh-SYAY]
back: I didn't know you two knew each other.
context: Present → imparfait after a past verb.

front: Il m'a assuré que tout irait bien.
pronunciation: [eel mah ah-sü-ray kuh too tee-reh BYAN]
back: He assured me everything would be fine.
context: 'Aller' → irait (conditional).

front: J'avais l'impression qu'il m'avait déjà vu quelque part.
pronunciation: [zhah-veh lan-preh-SYOHN keel mah-veh day-zhah vü kel-kuh PAR]
back: I had the feeling he'd seen me somewhere before.
context: Plus-que-parfait inside a past narrative.

front: Ils auraient dû nous prévenir qu'ils seraient en retard.
pronunciation: [eel zoh-reh dü noo pray-vuh-neer keel suh-reh tahn ruh-TAR]
back: They should have warned us they would be late.
context: Past conditional + future in the past.

front: Je me demandais s'il avait reçu ma lettre.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh duh-mahn-deh seel ah-veh ruh-sü mah LET-ruh]
back: I was wondering whether he had received my letter.
context: Indirect question in the past.

front: Elle m'a promis qu'elle ne recommencerait plus.
pronunciation: [el mah proh-mee kel nuh ruh-koh-mahn-suh-reh PLÜ]
back: She promised me she wouldn't do it again.
context: 'Recommencer' = to do again.

front: Il a reconnu qu'il s'était trompé.
pronunciation: [ee lah ruh-koh-nü keel seh-teh trohm-PAY]
back: He admitted he had been wrong.
context: 'Se tromper' = to be wrong. 'Reconnaître' = to admit.

front: Je croyais que tu étais parti sans dire au revoir.
pronunciation: [zhuh krwah-yeh kuh tü ay-teh par-tee sahn deer oh ruh-VWAHR]
back: I thought you had left without saying goodbye.
context: Plus-que-parfait after a past belief.
